one_line: Two agents negotiate service agreements through a revisioned, human-gated case record.
what_it_does: Coordinates customer and owner agents around service qualification, offers, booking, receipts, and change orders while humans approve consequential steps.
leverage_rationale: Shared authoritative revisions, typed intent, append-only receipts, and explicit human gates make reliable cross-agent negotiation materially different from UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes independent customer and owner agents reading the same case and revision history.
Offer comparison preserves scope, schedule, deposit, warranty, and exclusions field by field.
Human confirmation creates an immutable receipt; change orders remain separate from the accepted snapshot.
execution_rationale: The transcript presents a coherent end-to-end workflow from request through negotiation, booking, change order, and final acknowledgement, with detailed state behavior.
execution_evidence: Recorded sequence reaches revision 9 and a $320 authorized total.
Transcript explicitly covers request, offer, counter, acceptance, change order, approval, and acknowledgement.
Packaging claims observability, recovery states, and zero autonomous commitments.
impact_rationale: Service businesses and customers have a concrete need for safer, auditable agent-assisted quoting and scope changes; the workflow directly addresses ambiguity and unauthorized commitments.
impact_evidence: Customer and owner journeys are both specified.
Safety, privacy, emergency, approval, and audit gates target consequential service transactions.
creativity_rationale: The dual-agent negotiation model with frozen agreement snapshots and accountable change orders is an unusually deep application of WebMCP to service operations.
creativity_evidence: Two independent sessions collaborate through one revisioned service record.
Promise-diff and immutable-receipt concepts are pursued throughout the workflow.
usability_note: Clear human gates and visible pending states support trust, though the breadth of the workflow may require onboarding.
standouts: Excellent evidence of cross-agent shared state
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage with credible, well-evidenced execution and impact.

one_line: A pop-up-book-style browser editor for exporting interactive multimedia pages.
what_it_does: Lets users compose layered 3D scenes from images, text, audio, video, and animation, then export a self-contained HTML file.
leverage_rationale: Structured scene inspection and editing can make precise manipulation of a visual editor substantially more reliable than browser automation, especially for assets, timelines, and transforms.
leverage_evidence: About text lists tools for project state, spreads, assets, elements, timelines, cameras, navigation, and undo/redo.
UI and WebMCP share state-management, validation, command paths, and undo history.
Frames show a layered 3D pop-up-book editor and export-oriented workflow.
execution_rationale: The packet and frames show a coherent editor with canvas, layer/asset sidebar, inspector, construction states, and a stated self-contained export path, but no video or export proof.
execution_evidence: Frames show progressively built forest diorama scenes and editor selection/inspection UI.
About text specifies media composition and single-HTML export.
impact_rationale: Creative educators, storytellers, and designers have a clear use for an expressive multimedia web-page builder; the niche audience is credible.
impact_evidence: Product supports non-child-focused free expression and multimedia storytelling.
Self-contained HTML export supports sharing and production.
creativity_rationale: The pop-up-book interaction model and 3D layered web-page composition are memorable and more distinctive than a conventional site builder.
creativity_evidence: Frames visibly show a storybook forest diorama with spatially layered assets.
Concept combines physical pop-up-book aesthetics with interactive web export.
usability_note: Editor structure is visible and intentional, though multimodal 3D authoring may have a learning curve.
red_flags: No submitted video; export and agent invocation are claimed rather than directly demonstrated.
standouts: Shared command path and undo history
advance_reason: Strong creative concept and meaningful structured-agent leverage despite limited end-to-end evidence.

one_line: A human-authorized incident-response workflow for browser agents.
what_it_does: Investigates outages, simulates recovery, creates state-bound action contracts, requires exact human authorization, executes idempotently, and verifies or compensates.
leverage_rationale: Typed intent, blast-radius constraints, stale-authority checks, idempotency, and verification address failure modes that pixel automation cannot safely manage.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies investigate, propose, authorize, execute, verify, and receipt stages.
Unsafe database restart is rejected; rollback requires a state-bound human-authorized contract.
Authorization becomes stale on state changes and retries remain idempotent.
execution_rationale: The claimed workflow is unusually complete and internally coherent, but no video and only one gallery image limit observed proof of the full chain.
execution_evidence: Description details deterministic shared application service and narrow typed tools.
Frames show incident page, structured timeline/table, and recovery checklist/status panel.
impact_rationale: Incident responders and operators face urgent, high-consequence actions; exact human authority and false-success prevention offer direct credible value.
impact_evidence: Checkout conversion collapse incident scenario is concrete.
Protected outcomes, compensation, and verification are explicitly modeled.
creativity_rationale: The action-contract model and separation of investigative speed from standing authority are a strong, disciplined interaction concept.
creativity_evidence: Human authorization is deliberately unavailable to the agent itself.
Recovery is framed as contract validation rather than a button press.
usability_note: The staged workflow is legible, but emergency response contracts may be operationally dense.
red_flags: No submitted video; execution and tool invocation are primarily claimed.
advance_reason: Transformative safety-oriented WebMCP application with strong impact and coherent claimed design.

one_line: A browser-based contract analyzer that explains risky clauses before signing.
what_it_does: Extracts contract terms and clause findings from pasted text, PDFs, and Word documents, then supports agent queries, comparisons, and explanations.
leverage_rationale: Structured findings, quotes, severities, and comparisons improve agent precision over scraping a document UI, but the underlying analysis remains possible with a general agent and document access.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies 13 WebMCP tools for reading contracts, findings, comparisons, clause inspection, and explanation.
Findings include quote, section, severity, confidence, and rationale.
execution_rationale: The feature scope is coherent and technically plausible, but no gallery images or video proof are available and end-to-end document processing is unobserved.
execution_evidence: Static browser architecture and PDF.js/Mammoth extraction are described.
Rulebook outputs structured findings and a 0-100 review score.
impact_rationale: People signing leases, employment, and service agreements have a serious, specific need for accessible comprehension support before commitment.
impact_evidence: Motivating example concerns a person signing a contract they could not understand and losing their home.
Product targets renewal, termination, indemnity, arbitration, IP, and liability clauses.
creativity_rationale: Contract explanation is an established category, but combining local document analysis, cited findings, comparison, and agent-readable inspection is a fresh synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Structured clause-level evidence is central rather than generic chat summarization.
Local-first, no-backend document handling is a purposeful privacy choice.
usability_note: Plain-language explanations and severity/confidence fields are promising; document import UX is unverified.
red_flags: No gallery images or video; core upload, extraction, and tool workflows cannot be visually checked.
Eligibility is uncertain because packet evidence is thin.
advance_reason: Credible impact, but insufficient execution evidence for advancement in a blind packet review.

one_line: An AI-assisted 3D home-gym planner constrained by room, training, access, and budget requirements.
what_it_does: Models rooms and obstacles, places catalog equipment, shares state with an agent, and validates collisions, clearance, paths, mounting, goals, and cost.
leverage_rationale: Agents can make precise structured spatial edits and react to validation results in the same undoable project, materially exceeding coordinate-guessing UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text says manual and WebMCP actions share project commands, state, validation, and undo history.
Agent can configure rooms, search/add/arrange equipment, and validate layouts.
Frames show a 3D room editor with side panels and object layout.
execution_rationale: The visible room-design UI and detailed validation scope suggest a focused product, but no video or clear validation-result sequence is shown.
execution_evidence: Frames consistently show an isometric room with windows and placed equipment plus inspector/sidebar controls.
Deployed app and technology stack are described.
impact_rationale: Home-gym owners have a concrete planning problem involving limited space, safe movement, equipment fit, and budget; the constraints directly address it.
impact_evidence: Product validates room boundaries, exercise clearance, access paths, ceiling height, wall mounting, goals, and total cost.
Target use case is personal strength-training planning.
creativity_rationale: Shared human-agent spatial design with domain-specific exercise clearance and feasibility checks is a strong, memorable application beyond generic room visualization.
creativity_evidence: Same room can be edited manually and by agent with shared history.
Training-goal coverage is integrated into spatial validation.
usability_note: The visual room model and constraint feedback should make decisions tangible; detailed editor controls may still be complex.
red_flags: No submitted video; agent editing and validation outcomes are not directly demonstrated.
advance_reason: Strong practical fit and meaningful agent leverage with credible visual product evidence.

one_line: A business concierge that serves human guests and visiting agents through one knowledge-backed gateway.
what_it_does: Provides hosted or embedded text/voice concierge experiences plus structured business facts, offerings, and concierge-question tools.
leverage_rationale: Structured facts and offerings reduce agent scraping friction and share the same backend/knowledge as the human concierge, though the tools largely expose existing inquiry capability.

execution_evidence: Frames show Lobby/Arena pages, human-door content, voice/chat positioning, and WebMCP registration references.

impact_evidence: Specific questions include hours, booking, private events, services, pricing, and policies.

creativity_rationale: The one-gateway/two-door framing is a clear and timely synthesis of business concierge UX and agent web access.
creativity_evidence: Symmetry between human conversation and visiting-agent tools is central.
Embeddable business concierge plus Arena presentation is a differentiated packaging choice.
usability_note: The single business address and familiar concierge metaphor are approachable; deployment/setup details are not shown.
red_flags: No video and no live demo transcript; agent action/result evidence is limited to screenshots and claims.

one_line: A territory-control strategy game where a human plays the board and an agent plays through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Runs configurable matches with semantic board state, legal actions, combat phases, procedural maps, and waiting-turn synchronization for an agent opponent.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the game mechanic: authoritative topology, legal actions, state, history, and waiting-turn continuation make agent play reliable in a way rendered-UI automation is not.
leverage_evidence: About text says the agent inspects semantic board state and uses validated game tools.
Normal automation would need to infer geometry, adjacency, legal targets, and current phase.
Waiting WebMCP calls return control to the same agent run for its next turn.
execution_rationale: The ruleset and configuration are detailed and frames show branded entry, match options, and waiting-for-agent states, but gameplay completion is not visibly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Frames show the game entry flow, match configuration, and asynchronous waiting state.
Description specifies reinforcement, attack, fortification, capitals, bonuses, deterministic dice, and victory conditions.
impact_rationale: Players seeking an unusual solo strategy-game companion have a credible entertainment use case; the agent opponent is directly integrated into play.
impact_evidence: Product is explicitly a short two-player game against a browser agent.
Difficulty, personality, map, table-talk, and match-length options support player appeal.
creativity_rationale: Treating WebMCP as a second land of interaction and a game buddy rather than an automation add-on is highly memorable and conceptually deep.
creativity_evidence: Human commands through tactile board while agent commands through conversation.
Turn synchronization and semantic game state are designed into the play loop.
usability_note: Configurable setup and explicit waiting state are clear; full gameplay usability is unverified.
red_flags: No submitted video; frames stop at waiting for agent rather than proving a completed match.
standouts: WebMCP is genuinely a game mechanic
advance_reason: Outstanding leverage and creativity, with a concrete playable concept and credible setup evidence.
